# services/packs/figures/

## Purpose
The board pack's figure supply and the gate that refuses a pack that does not reconcile. Nothing here computes a statement figure: each is copied from the service that owns it and recorded with where it came from.

## Main pieces
- `packFigureSet.ts`: `buildPackFigureSet` reads actual, prior-period and budget figures once. A prior or budget read that the database refuses degrades to an absence (own savepoint, `isFailedRead`); a defect is re-thrown.
- `packFigureProvenance.ts`: `PackFigure` (`money | pct | ratio | days`) and `PackFigureProvenance`. Every printed figure records a `source` (the service call and field). A null value must carry a non-blank `unavailable` reason.
- `packMetricReads.ts`: the one reading of any metric two pages both show (debtor/creditor days, debt-to-equity, operating profit, investing cash flow, `readOverCurrentLiabilities`). Two readings of one source is how pages 3 and 9 come to disagree, so pages call these, not their own arithmetic.
- `packFigureIntegrity.ts` (`assertPackIntegrity`, the last act of `buildBoardPackPages`), with `packStatementIntegrity` / `packStatementIdentities` (statements foot, six declared identities), `packBlockIntegrity` / `packMattersIntegrity` (bridges foot, `prior` columns, pages 4 and 11 agree), `packWaterfallIntegrity`, `packProseIntegrity`, `packLocatedFigures` (the walk of every printed figure).
- `packIntegrityRefusal.ts`: `integrityRefusal` turns failures into a `PackRefusal` (engineer message plus a reader sentence per `IntegrityCheck`; a `Record` over the union, so a new check needs its wording).
- `packTextLayer.ts`: a test-time check that the rendered PDF's text layer contains the figures and furniture (`tests/unit/print/packTextLayer.test.ts`); there is no production caller.

## Rules
- **Refusal contract:** the gate throws `PackRefusal`; only that becomes a 422 with its `userMessage`. Throwing a bare `Error` from the compose makes a 500 and tells the person nothing.
- Every printed figure resolves through provenance at the value the page carries; one source printed twice prints identically (exact, no tolerance). A source issued twice with two values fails, so sources must be unique per item.
- Tolerances: `MONEY_TOLERANCE` (one cent), `PCT_TOLERANCE` (one basis point), `RATIO_TOLERANCE` 0.0051 (the engine rounds a ratio twice; wider shows a wrong second decimal). Pinned from both sides.
- A quotient must state its working both ways: a `money` figure carrying a numerator/denominator, or a `pct`/`ratio` carrying none, is refused. `days` is not a quotient format.
- A null figure with an `unavailable` reason is skipped by the arithmetic checks, never failed. Liquidity ratios with no current liabilities are not meaningful, not 0.
- Do not sum a table's line rows into its subtotal row; statements print cost of sales positive then subtract it. A mid-statement subtotal bar is `kind: 'subtotal'` and is checked on its `end`.
- Both bridges carry a NAMED plug (`Unexplained movement`, `Other, not separately captured`), marked `uncaptured: true`. A plug over `UNCAPTURED_SHARE_LIMIT` of the smaller of endpoint and movement must carry `disproportionatePlugSentence`.
- EBITDA equals the operating line (no depreciation is supplied) and every page reads operating profit via `OPERATING_PROFIT_SOURCE`.
- The comparative is the period the pack claims: `comparativePeriod` holds the label and the window, and the gate re-derives the label from the window.
- `checkProse` refuses printed plumbing: identifiers, spec clauses, `(s)` plurals, machine timestamps, sentinels. It does not read ledger text a person typed.
- Do not add a check without a test that goes red when the production code is mutated.
